Plants that may grow into each other can be nudged apart: “Nudge apart” moves the newer one, or the one you’ve selected, away from the other just far enough that they no longer overlap at their usual size. It stays in its bed and isn’t pushed into a third plant; where there’s no room, it says so and leaves it be. Undo puts it back. It’s in the crowding notice as you place a plant, in Warnings and in the plant’s details.

Swap from a warning opens the plant list already filtered for what went wrong, with a line saying why: the sun where it’s planted, plants hardy in your zone, the kids and pets in the yard, or a width that fits the spot. They’re ordinary filters you can take off, and they’re gone the next time you open the plant list. Swap is in each warning in Warnings and in the plant’s details.

Swapping a plant that’s too big for its spot lists the smaller forms of the same plant first, such as a compact cultivar, by the sizes their sources give, smallest first and each saying whether it fits; then the rest. Never other plants that only look alike.
A plant’s details say when it’s wider than its bed, with a way to swap it for a smaller one.
